summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, gastroparesis, and recent MSSA bacteremia and C. difficile infection was readmitted one day after discharge for diabetic ketoacidosis. She presented with severe hyperglycemia (glucose 903), anion gap of 19, and epigastric pain, but no vomiting. She was treated in the ICU with an insulin drip, which resolved the DKA within 12 hours. Hemodialysis was performed on two consecutive days for metabolic clearance and fluid management. Persistent hyperglycemia on her prior insulin regimen led to dose adjustments: Lantus increased to 10 units morning and 14 units night, and Humalog modified to include a fixed 4-unit pre-meal dose plus a sliding scale. Her hypertension was managed with increased labetalol, and furosemide was discontinued. She continued antibiotics for MSSA (cefazolin and vancomycin locks) and C. difficile (metronidazole). She remained on her home medications for gastroparesis and was discharged home in stable condition, tolerating a full diet, with detailed instructions on insulin adjustment, medication adherence, and follow-up.
